item.title: SBOLinside: Episode 2 with Prof. Anil Wipat
item.description:
We are excited to share that the second episode of our video podcast series, SBOLinside, is now live!

Following our debut with Prof. Herbert Sauro, this new installment dives deeper into the technical challenges of biology data exchange, community governance, and how modern data standards intersect with artificial intelligence.

Episode 2: How Do We Integrate Data into SBOL?

In this episode, host Erik Kubaczka welcomes Prof. Anil Wipat, AI Director at Prozomix and Professor at Newcastle University. Having served as the second chair of SBOL starting in late 2015, Anil brings a unique perspective spanning molecular microbiology, bioinformatics, computing, and commercial biotechnology.

Here is a brief sneak peek of what Anil discusses in this episode:

  • Transition to Open Governance: How the community established an elected steering committee and introduced SBOL Enhancement Proposals (SEPs)— an open, RFC-style proposal process that empowered anyone to propose improvements and directly shape the standard.
  • SBOL 1 to SBOL 2 (and Joining COMBINE): How SBOL expanded beyond basic sequences and components to capture molecular interactions and functions, while formally joining COMBINE to connect with the broader bioinformatics and biotechnology standards ecosystem.
  • Simplifying Towards SBOL 3: Why the transition toward SBOL 3 addressed community feedback about steep learning curves by streamlining data models and APIs, making it significantly easier for software developers to build tools.
  • Standards as Contracts for AI Agents: Drawing from his current industry work in enzyme engineering, Anil shares a forward-looking vision of how standards like SBOL can serve as communication contracts for autonomous AI agents collaborating across the Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle.

Watch Now!

You can watch the full interview on our YouTube channel.

Follow us on LinkedIn and check back on the SBOL Blog for upcoming episodes and community updates!

What’s Next? In our next episode, we will be joined by Prof. Chris Myers to explore how software tools can make working with SBOL seamless and what lies ahead for standard usability. Stay tuned!

item.title: Introducing SBOLinside: Our New Video Podcast
item.description:
Alongside our day-to-day editorial work, we have been developing something special for the SBOL community. We asked ourselves: how can we offer deeper insights into SBOL and our organization while making it easier for the community to follow our ongoing work? Our answer is SBOLinside.

SBOLinside is a video podcast format specifically focusing on providing inside stories from our work on SBOL and our organization. The series will feature interviews with key figures driving the standard forward, including members of the Steering Committee, the Editors, the Chair, and many more. We will also present what we are currently working on and share ways on how you can actively engage with and support the Synthetic Biology Open Language (SBOL). The episodes of SBOLinside will be released on our YouTube channel and announced on LinkedIn and our blog.

Is there a specific aspect of SBOL you would love to learn more about? Reach out to us and we will be happy to consider your topic for a future episode.

item.title: Welcome to the SBOL Blog
item.description:
Welcome to the SBOL community blog. This is a space for developers, researchers, and users of the Synthetic Biology Open Language to share insights, tutorials, tools, and perspectives.

Whether you are building a new library, publishing a design workflow, or exploring SBOL for the first time, this blog is a venue to connect with the broader community and learn from one another.

Stay tuned for upcoming posts from contributors across the community.

item.title: COMBINE 2026 — Workshop at Keele University, UK
item.description:
The Computational Modeling in Biology Network (COMBINE) is an initiative to coordinate the development of community standards and formats in systems biology, synthetic biology, and related fields.

COMBINE 2026 will be hosted at Keele University, UK, from 7–10 September 2026. The workshop includes talks, tutorials, and breakout sessions for detailed discussions about standards, related efforts, and tools.

Full details — including venue, travel, and accommodation — are available at co.mbine.org/events.

Registration

Registration is now open. In-person attendance requires a two-step process: first complete the Google form, then pay the registration fee via the Keele University website.

Abstract Submission

Submissions are open for:

  • Talks
  • Tutorials
  • Breakout sessions
  • Lightning talks
  • Posters

Important Dates

Milestone Date
Submission deadline (all categories) 19 July 2026
Notification of acceptance 26 July 2026
Registration deadline 2 August 2026
Late registration deadline 23 August 2026
COMBINE 2026 7–10 September 2026

Topics of Interest

  • Data exchange, pipelines, and model standards for systems and synthetic biology
  • Visualization and graphical notation standards for systems and synthetic biology
  • Standards for sharing and analyzing biological pathway data
  • Standards for computational biological models and modeling support
  • Metadata description and model annotation in COMBINE standard formats
  • Implementation of COMBINE standards in tools, databases, and other resources
  • Integrated model and data management for systems and synthetic biology
  • Standardization of Artificial Intelligence approaches in biological modeling
  • Emerging standardization needs and multicellular modeling
  • Community aspects of COMBINE
